title: Paloma and the Ledger
premise: In the winter of 1912, Mirabel Vane drives for the formidable suffragist Edith Marchmont, reading her correspondence in secret and believing himself a bystander to history. When the flood season closes the bridge out of Ashcombe Vale, he is trapped among the household he serves — and discovers that Edith's letters conceal a family ledger of debts, inheritances, and one berth on the last mail steamer south before the roads fail entirely. As fever spreads through the valley and old grievances surface, Mirabel must decide who deserves escape: Edith's estranged daughter, the loyal housekeeper's sick son, or himself. In choosing to give up his own place and forging the ledger instead, he learns that history happens to whoever stays behind to write it down.
about_author: Felix Thornbury is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing private letters in country-house collections. He writes historical fiction about the people history forgot to name.

chapters.title: The Man Behind the Wheel
chapters.summary: Mirabel Vane, chauffeur and self-appointed invisible man, delivers Edith Marchmont's post after quietly reading each letter. POV: Mirabel. Establishes his philosophy of detachment and his sharp eye for what people hide. Emotional beat: comfortable loneliness mistaken for safety.

chapters.title: Letters Worth Stealing
chapters.summary: A letter from a solicitor hints at an inheritance dispute within the Marchmont family; Mirabel pockets knowledge he shouldn't have. POV: Mirabel, with a brief interlude of Edith dictating to her secretary. Emotional beat: the first crack in his neutrality — curiosity curdling into complicity.

chapters.title: The Bridge Bell
chapters.summary: Autumn rains swell the river; the bell rings to warn that the bridge will close within days. The household scrambles to finish errands. POV: alternating Mirabel and the housekeeper, Ruth Callow. Emotional beat: urgency disguised as routine; everyone assumes they'll be on the right side of the water.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Says
chapters.summary: Mirabel finds Edith's leather ledger: debts owed, favors banked, and a single reserved berth on the last steamer south, unnamed. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: vertigo — the discovery that the woman he serves has been keeping score of human lives.

chapters.title: Ruth's Boy
chapters.summary: Ruth's son Tobias shows the first signs of the fever moving up the valley. She begs Mirabel, as the only one with a motorcar, to consider driving him overland before the pass snows shut. POV: Ruth. Emotional beat: maternal desperation meeting Mirabel's instinct to stay uninvolved.

chapters.title: The Daughter Returns
chapters.summary: Edith's estranged daughter, Clemence, arrives unannounced from London, ostensibly to reconcile — really, Mirabel suspects, for the inheritance. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: the household's careful equilibrium tilts; Mirabel recognizes a fellow reader of other people's mail.

chapters.title: Dinner with Knives
chapters.summary: A tense dinner where Edith, Clemence, and Ruth perform civility while circling the question of the berth. Mirabel serves the wine and hears everything. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: dark comedy giving way to dread as the stakes are made explicit.

chapters.title: Fever in the Vale
chapters.summary: The doctor confirms the fever has reached the village below; the bridge is now closed by order, not just season. Quarantine talk begins. POV: Ruth. Emotional beat: the abstract deadline becomes flesh — Tobias worsens.

chapters.title: Clemence's Bargain
chapters.summary: Clemence privately offers Mirabel money to put her mother on the next train and herself on the steamer, revealing she knows about his letter-reading. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: blackmail as intimacy — being truly seen for the first time, and it costs him.

chapters.title: Edith's Confession
chapters.summary: Edith, sensing the end approaching, tells Mirabel why the berth exists: it was meant for her late son, and she cannot bear to choose its new owner. POV: Edith. Emotional beat: the titan reduced to grief; Mirabel's contempt softens into something like love.

chapters.title: The Pass Closes
chapters.summary: Snow seals the mountain route; the steamer berth is now the only way out for anyone. Mirabel tests the overland track by night and turns back. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: claustrophobia — every door but one has shut.

chapters.title: Tobias Takes a Turn
chapters.summary: Tobias deteriorates sharply; Ruth stops asking nicely and starts planning to take the berth by force if needed. POV: Ruth. Emotional beat: love hardening into ruthlessness, and Mirabel understanding it completely.

chapters.title: The Forged Page
chapters.summary: Mirabel, a skilled hand with pen and ink from years of practice, secretly alters the ledger to make the berth read as transferable. He tells himself it's administrative, not moral. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: the quiet thrill and horror of becoming an author of fate.

chapters.title: Clemence Finds Out
chapters.summary: Clemence catches Mirabel with the altered ledger and, instead of exposing him, asks to be written in — offering again to keep his secret. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: temptation wearing a friendly face; the found-family theme sharpened by its counterfeit.

chapters.title: Night Watch
chapters.summary: Mirabel sits up with Tobias through the worst hours, reading aloud from the letters he once stole, including one from Tobias's dead father. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: tenderness breaking through his armor; the boy becomes a person, not a case.

chapters.title: Edith Decides
chapters.summary: Edith announces her choice at breakfast: the berth goes to Clemence, to mend the bloodline. Ruth erupts; the household fractures. POV: Edith. Emotional beat: authority wielded as apology, and failing.

chapters.title: The Storm
chapters.summary: The great storm hits; the river takes the mill, the lights fail, and the steamer's departure moves up a day. Everyone must pack tonight. POV: rotating — Mirabel, Ruth, Clemence. Emotional beat: chaos stripping away pretense; true priorities exposed.

chapters.title: The Last Berth
chapters.summary: At the dock road's edge, Mirabel reveals the forged ledger: the berth is now assigned to Tobias, with Ruth accompanying as guardian. He confronts Edith with the truth of all her accounting. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: climax — sacrifice declared, consequences accepted.

chapters.title: What Clemence Does
chapters.summary: Given the chance to expose the forgery and reclaim the berth, Clemence instead burns the original page and chooses to stay with her mother. POV: Clemence. Emotional beat: redemption earned through renunciation; the found family forms around a shared crime of mercy.

chapters.title: The Steamer Whistle
chapters.summary: Tobias and Ruth depart through the rain; Mirabel watches from the bridge ruins, having given up his only exit. Edith stands beside him without reproach. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: grief and release entwined; invisibility finally surrendered.

chapters.title: Spring Thaw
chapters.summary: Weeks later, the fever breaks and the bridge reopens. The household, diminished and remade, plants the spring garden together; Edith begins a new ledger titled 'Owed.' POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: quiet reconstruction; debts reframed as bonds.

chapters.title: The First Letter
chapters.summary: Mirabel writes his own letter for the first time — to Ruth, enclosing a photograph — and delivers it unopened. History, he understands now, belongs to those who stay and tell it. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: resolution — the reader of letters becomes their author.
